parts:
On Sun, 2012-04-01 at 00:46 -0700, Chris wrote:
> Hi all,
> I've been trying for a week to work around this error.
>
>
> #####
> file: smtp-taucs.c hgid: 64e669042e54 date: Fri Mar 16 12:57:24 2012
> +0100
> Function: GMRFLib_factorise_sparse_matrix_TAUCS(), Line: 780, Thread:
> 0
> Fail to factorize Q. I will try to fix it...


When we get 'Fail to factorize Q' it means that the precision matrix is
numerically singular. In most cases it is not, but it can still be so
numerically for some ''almost ill-defined models''.

When the precision matrix *is* singular, this is usually due to the
improper default prior for the intercept, so setting
control.fixed=list(prec.intecept=0.001), or similar, will solve the
issue.

the intrinsic models, are almost singular, as they have a constr=TRUE
default, which ensure they are not. However, numerically, they are
computed without the constraint and then we correct for the constraint.
this means there are some small epsilons around to make non-sinuglar.
This the argument 'diagonal=' in the 'f()', which is default 1e-6 for
intrinsic models. This constant can be to small in some cases.


so, increasing the diagonal argument and setting a proper prior for the
intercept, solves the issue.

set.seed (1)
n <- 500
t <- 25 ## n observations per loc
y <- rnorm(n*t)
x <- y+rnorm(n*t)
t2 <- rep(1:t,each=n)
id <- rep(1:n,each=t)

data <- data.frame("y"=y, "x"=x, "t2"=t2, "id"=id)
A = matrix(runif(n^2), n, n)
B <-inla.matrix2graph(A) # tried as a grap

diag.eps = 1e-4
test <- inla(y~x+f(id, model="besag", graph=B, diagonal=diag.eps)+
f(t2, model="rw2", diagonal = diag.eps),
data=data, family="gaussian",
verbose=T,
control.fixed = list(prec.intercept = 0.01))


rho = 0.9 ## sparse matrix example
Q = toeplitz(c(1+rho^2, -rho, rep(0, n-3), -rho)) / (1-rho^2)
Q = inla.as.dgTMatrix(Q)

diag.eps = 1e-3
test2 <- inla(y~x+f(id, model="besag", graph=Q, diagonal=diag.eps) +
f(t2, model="rw2", diagonal=diag.eps),
data=data, family="gaussian",
verbose=TRUE,
keep=TRUE,
control.fixed = list(prec.intercept = 0.01))

Hello,
I am having a similar problem. In my case the precision of the intercept does not seem to be the problem.

I changed the diagonal value and it runs, but I am not sure to what extent the model itself is different. Estimates vary considerably when I change the diag values. What criteria should I follow for this?

the model goes like this

f.rw1 <- y ~ 0 + b0 + b1  +
  f(idx, model=spde, diagonal=***, group=idx.group,
    control.group=list(model='rw1'))

A similar "ar1" model run with no problem.

Thank you!
Iosu

On Thu, 2014-09-25 at 03:29 -0700, Iosu Paradinas wrote:
> Hello,
> I am having a similar problem. In my case the precision of the
> intercept does not seem to be the problem.
>
> I changed the diagonal value and it runs, but I am not sure to what
> extent the model itself is different. Estimates vary considerably when
> I change the diag values. What criteria should I follow for this?
>
> the model goes like this
>
> f.rw1 <- y ~ 0 + b0 + b1 +
> f(idx, model=spde, diagonal=***, group=idx.group,
> control.group=list(model='rw1'))

> file: smtp-taucs.c hgid: 64e669042e54 date: Fri Mar 16 12:57:24 2012
> +0100
> Function: GMRFLib_factorise_sparse_matrix_TAUCS(), Line: 780, Thread:
> 0
> Fail to factorize Q. I will try to fix it...

says that the current precision matrix (including the contribution from
the likelihood), is numerical singular. By definition, it is not, but in
pratice it can be.

the argument

f(..., diagonal=...)

is used to add a small diagonal value to the precision matrix for this
model component. its main usage is for intrinsic models like

f(.., model="rw1", constr=TRUE, diagonal=..)

where the default diag-value is about 1e-6. sinced this value is used to
make the model proper before conditiong, then as along as 1/diagonal is
much larger than the posterior variance of that model component, then
the effect is neglible.




H

--
Håvard Rue
